Chapter 13. The Cross and the Invitation to Rest.
You know, in a world that seems to run on busy schedules and endless to-do lists, the idea of real rest almost feels out of reach. It’s easy to think of rest as some kind of luxury—something we’ll get to eventually, if we have time. But what if rest isn’t just a rare treat? What if it’s actually at the heart of what the cross offers us?
Picture this: it’s late, you’re lying awake, and your mind just won’t stop spinning. Or maybe you’re a parent, stretched so thin you feel like you’re never quite enough. We’ve all been there. The cross speaks right into that exhaustion. It quietly tells us, “You’re not measured by what you achieve. You’re held by a love that doesn’t depend on your performance.” Rest isn’t laziness—it’s a kind of trust.
Most of us struggle to slow down, don’t we? Maybe we’re a little afraid of what might surface in the quiet. But here’s something to pay attention to: the cross assures us that we are safe, even with our fears and failures. We can bring them into the light, and we won’t be turned away.
The book shares stories about people who, after years of pushing themselves, finally discovered a deeper kind of rest—not just for the body, but for the soul. Think about a leader who decides it’s okay to step back and let others share the load. Or a caregiver who finally lets themselves be cared for, even for just a moment.
Rest, shaped by the cross, isn’t about running away or avoiding life. It’s about renewal. It’s making space for grace, for gratitude, and for joy to slip back in. The cross becomes the place where we can lay down what we just can’t carry anymore, and receive what we could never earn on our own.
So if you’re feeling overwhelmed or worn out, maybe this is the invitation you’ve been waiting for. Come, rest. You don’t have to carry it all—there’s a deeper peace waiting for you.
